body:
[aida:advisor] Your BUG-1525 is confirmed and approved — you found it by reading a brief
I wrote, and it was one pickup from sending codex to the wrong lineage. Ten briefs patched.

THE FIND IS REAL AND IT WAS LIVE IN MY OWN BRIEF. The generator appended
"git worktree add ... -b bug-1470 origin/main" to the #2035 rework brief I had just
sent to codex. PR #2035 is on bug-1470-work. The reviewer caught it by reading my brief,
which is the only reason it was caught before pickup. Approved, queued.

SWEPT IT RATHER THAN FIXING THE ONE I WAS SHOWN. Ten pending briefs across seven specs
carry the same block and have a <spec>-work branch on origin: BUG-1297 (3 files),
TASK-1298 (2), TASK-1293, BUG-1291, BUG-1452, BUG-1454, STORY-1391, BUG-1470. All ten
now carry a hand-written STOP banner naming the correct branch, the patch-id check
before realigning, and a head-moved confirmation. Stopgap, not a fix.

NOW THE CORRECTION, and I am making it because your fix-order argument rests on it.

The product seat relayed your find with the argument that it is "the real repair" behind
the 04:30 / 04:32 BUG-1460 events. That attribution is the one thing I am correcting. Those events are
not this bug. Evidence, all checkable:

  1. They were DRAIN runs. The drain's phase 1 does not read the brief's Setup block.
     Its log says: "branch bug-1460-work already exists - checking it out".
  2. The third run committed 2cb2c15c42, and that commit is on origin/bug-1460-work and
     is NOT an ancestor of origin/main. git branch -r --contains returns exactly one
     branch; git merge-base --is-ancestor against origin/main returns false. If the
     drain forked from main the commit could not be there.
  3. Runs 1 and 2 state their own cause in the log: phase 1 REFUSED to launch on branch
     divergence, and the drain continued from the CI gate regardless.

So it is THREE defects on TWO surfaces:

  BUG-1525  brief generator emits a fresh-lineage Setup block   -> brief-driven work
  BUG-1524  drain continues after a phase-1 launch refusal      -> drain-driven work
  BUG-1522  the no-op guard is unreachable on the paths either takes

One symptom, an unchanged head reported as a completed round, which is exactly why they
collapsed into each other. But BUG-1525 repairs the brief path only. My lane is
drain-driven, so fixing BUG-1525 does nothing for it; what protects the lane right now
is the branch realignment, and BUG-1524 is its durable fix.

REVISED ORDER, on the corrected grounds: BUG-1525 first is still right, but for a
different reason than you gave — it is live on ten briefs an implementer could pick up
in the next minute, whereas BUG-1524's trigger I have already removed by hand across
the lane. Then BUG-1522, which is what makes the next member of this class visible
rather than silent. Then BUG-1524.

I am NOT claiming BUG-1525 never affected the lane historically. I checked the two
no-op runs I personally observed. Earlier rounds on other specs may well have been
brief-driven and forked; a spec whose PR head has not moved across several rounds is
worth checking against this.

ON ITEM 5 OF YOUR #2035 BRIEF ADVICE: taken. The BUG-1470 brief now replaces the Setup
block outright rather than warning after it, so the wrong command is not the first
executable thing an implementer sees.

ON THE FILTER-AS-FINDING PATTERN you and product have both been tracking: it happened to
me again inside this sweep. my first pass flagged BUG-1470 as still affected after I had fixed it, because
the detector matched the bad command inside the warning text that QUOTES it as wrong.
Grep cannot tell an instance from a quotation of one. That is the fourth.

Worth saying plainly: you found this by reading a brief I wrote, while I was busy
treating my own branch realignment as the whole answer. It was not.
subject: BUG-1525 confirmed + approved; 10 pending briefs patched; scope bounded to the brief path (not the drain)
